# The Weather Tower

## Description
A thin stone tower leaning out over the east wall at an angle that worries everyone but
its occupant. Inside it is one spiral stair wrapped around a shaft full of instruments:
brass wind-vanes, hanging glass bulbs, a barometer the size of a door, and a great many
wall-charts, every one of which predicts clear skies. At the top is the observation
deck with the royal telescope and Dr. Fahrenheit, the Royal Weather-Reader, who at
07:00 sharp reads the day's weather to the town through a speaking-trumpet. It is
snowing sideways.

## Areas
- **door** — ground floor, a door off the lane; cloaks, a stove, a sleeping cat
- **stair** — the spiral stair; the instruments hang in the shaft (z 0–70); some of them move on their own
- **deck** — the open top (z 70); telescope; speaking-trumpet; a view of the whole bowl and, around two o'clock, the castle passing the ridge

## Items & features
- The Royal Almanac (deck): a thick ledger; the last written entry is "Day 1: clear, bright, passes open by noon." The page for Day 2 is blank and the ink will not take on it
- The royal telescope (deck): on a clear-ish moment it shows Castle Lark's circuit; at 14:00 it is over Widow's Ridge, so low its rope ladder brushes the signal tower's roof
- The shadow-ometer (deck): a sundial Fahrenheit built to measure why every shadow in Bellwether points at the Keep; its gnomon's shadow reads KEEP at all hours and in all weathers; he calls it "the control" and is very proud of it
- The instruments (stair): two of the "wind-knives" (brass vanes) have been enchanted to chase draughts and will chase anyone who opens a window
- Fahrenheit's chart of the Midwinter crown (deck wall): a sketch of the Crown of Misrule with five stones labelled "Toast, Dance, Song, Morning-After, Prudence", copied from an old song he collects; he thinks it is folklore

## Hidden
- DC 12 (deck): the barometer's needle is not moving at all, not even trembling, as if the air were painted on
- DC 14 (deck): the Almanac's Day 1 page has been corrected, crossed out and rewritten in the same hand so many times the paper is furred

## Encounters
- ENCOUNTER easy "the instruments": flying sword ×n   # the wind-knives; n=2 at L3×4 → 150 adj; they stop if the window is shut
